Where is Jackson and how is the city laid out?

Jackson is Mississippi's capital and its most populous city, on the Pearl River in the middle of the state. It is mostly in northeastern Hinds County, and it shares the county seat role with Raymond. Small pieces of the city lie in Rankin County, where the airport sits, and in Madison County, where Tougaloo College is.

The city covers about 113 square miles, so it is large and varied. Ridgeland is to the north, Flowood and Richland to the east, Byram to the south and Clinton to the west. Interstates 55 and 20 cross near downtown, with Interstate 220 and U.S. 49, 51 and 80 filling in the grid. Union Station downtown serves Amtrak's City of New Orleans, Greyhound and the city's buses.

The 2020 census counted 153,701 residents, down 11.42 percent from 173,514 in 2010, the largest decline of any major U.S. city that decade. For a seller, a shrinking city means that location inside Jackson matters a great deal, and the same street can feel very different from one ward to the next.

What is the situation with Jackson's water system?

The water system is under federal court supervision, and sellers should know how that is described officially. The EPA says the Jackson system has more than 71,000 water connections, and that extensive repairs continue at both treatment plants and in the distribution network. In the 2022 crisis, tens of thousands of people were left without running water for weeks.

On November 29, 2022, the federal court entered an Interim Stipulated Order agreed to by the EPA, the Department of Justice, the Mississippi State Department of Health and the City. It appointed Edward "Ted" Henifin, through JXN Water, as Interim Third-Party Manager to operate the system and carry out a list of priority projects. The EPA reports that repairs to distribution leaks reduced average daily demand by 25 percent and that corrosion control treatment was completed at the J.H. Fewell plant.

What does that mean for a seller? Buyers may ask about water pressure, boil water notices and plumbing. Keep recent water bills, note any past notices, and be ready to answer. JXN Water posts bill payment, customer service and boil water information, and the Health Department posts compliance reports. An as-is cash buyer does not need your plumbing to impress a lender.

Who are the major employers and schools in Jackson?

The state government, a medical center, a school district and a car plant anchor the local economy. According to the city's own information cited on Wikipedia, the top three employers are the University of Mississippi Medical Center, Jackson Public Schools and Nissan North America. C Spire and Amazon have a large presence in the area too.

Jackson Public Schools covers most of the city, but some Hinds County addresses fall in other districts, so verify your school district rather than guessing.

What weather and ground conditions affect a Jackson house?

Jackson has a humid subtropical climate with year-round rain and a strong storm season. Average annual precipitation is 57.35 inches, thunder is heard on about 70 days a year, and severe thunderstorms can bring large hail, damaging winds and tornadoes. The F5 Candlestick Park tornado of March 3, 1966 killed 19 people in South Jackson.

Much of Jackson is built on acidic silt loam soil, with loess topsoil in the western sections and silt loam in the central flood plain. The Pearl River runs along the eastern edge of the city, and the Ross Barnett Reservoir lies to the northeast.

Practical points for an owner:

  • Hail and wind claims are part of a roof's history, so keep claim paperwork.
  • Foundation movement and drainage problems are common reasons buyers ask for repair credits in silty soils.
  • Check the flood designation for properties near the river or creeks before you assume insurance costs.

How does Jackson enforce property standards?

The city's Office of Code Services enforces the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code with local amendments. Its Community Improvement division says it seeks voluntary compliance, uses the courts as a last resort, and uses federal, state and local funds to fix violations by absentee owners. The city is divided into eight enforcement beats, each with an assigned officer.

Council packets and minutes show how it works in practice. The council passes resolutions declaring particular parcels a menace to public health, safety and welfare under Section 21-19-11 of the Mississippi Code, and authorizes cleaning or demolition. Ask the city's code office whether any cleanup or demolition costs have been assessed against your parcel.

Rental owners have another obligation. Jackson relaunched its rental registration program, which requires a local agent who can act for the owner and results in a Rental Certificate. The city notes there are now more rentals than owner-occupied units. If you own a rental here, check that it is registered before you sell, and tell any buyer.

When are Hinds County property taxes due, and what happens at closing?

Hinds County mails tax statements in the first week of December, and payment in full is due on or before February 1. The county applies a half percent per month penalty to taxes paid after February 1, including installment payments, and judges lateness by postmark. If you do not receive a bill, the county tax collector's phone is (601) 968-6591.

One detail often surprises sellers. The county says the name of the owner as of January 1 is the name that appears on the tax statement, which is why a buyer may see the previous owner listed on a receipt. Taxes are normally prorated between buyer and seller at closing, and your title company can explain how.

Delinquent properties can be sold at the tax sale, and Hinds County publishes delinquent and tax sale lists. The state allows tax sales on the first Monday in April and the last Monday in August, so confirm the county's actual schedule.

What are the choices for selling a Jackson house quickly?

You can list it, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer, and in Jackson the condition of the property and its paperwork often decide which route works. A covered seller must deliver a written property condition disclosure statement before title transfers under Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code. Be accurate on it, since buyers may ask about water service and storm history.

Inherited houses, vacant houses, houses with open code cases and rentals with registration problems are all common cash sale situations. A cash buyer can take the house as is and handle city notices after purchase, but you should still pay off liens from proceeds and tell the buyer about any known violations.

Compare offers by what you keep, not by the headline number. Ask for the terms in writing, ask who pays closing costs, and take your time. We make no price promises, and you are free to turn an offer down.

Jackson is mostly in Hinds County, where it shares the county seat with Raymond. Small portions of the city extend into Rankin County and Madison County.

They are due on or before February 1. A penalty of one half percent per month applies after that date, and a postmark after February 1 counts as late.

Is Jackson's water safe, and does it affect selling?

The EPA reports ongoing repairs and a court-ordered third-party manager operating the system, and JXN Water posts boil water notices. Buyers may ask about it, so keep your bills and answer questions honestly.

Do I have to register a rental house in Jackson before selling it?

The city requires registration of rental units and issues a Rental Certificate. Check your status with the Office of Code Services and disclose any problem to a buyer.

Can I sell a Jackson house with code violations?

Yes. Open violations and any city cleanup liens are usually resolved or paid from the proceeds at closing, so ask the code office what is outstanding. Selling as is to a cash buyer is a common way to handle it.

Where is Gulfport and how is the city laid out?

Gulfport is a port city on the Mississippi Sound in Harrison County, and it is one of the county's two seats. The 2020 census counted 72,926 residents, which made it the second-largest city in Mississippi after Jackson.

The city covers 64.2 square miles, of which 56.9 square miles is land. Interstate 10 crosses the middle of town, U.S. 90 runs along the coast through downtown, and U.S. 49 ends in Gulfport from the north. The city has seven wards and a strong mayor-council government.

The map is the product of annexation. In 1965 Gulfport took in the older settlements of Mississippi City and Handsboro, and in December 1993 it annexed 33 square miles to the north, including the historic community of Turkey Creek. A house in Gulfport can therefore sit near the beach, along a bayou, or in a newer northern subdivision, and each setting brings different insurance, flood and repair questions.

For land records, Harrison County has two judicial districts. The Chancery Clerk's first district office for recording and redemption is at 1801 23rd Avenue in Gulfport.

What shaped Gulfport's housing stock?

Storms and railroads shaped it more than anything else. William H. Hardy picked the site in 1887 as the coastal end of the Gulf and Ship Island Railroad, and the city incorporated on July 28, 1898. By 1906 the port was shipping more than 293 million feet of lumber, which made Gulfport the largest lumber export city in the country for a time.

Two hurricanes reset the building stock. Camille in August 1969 pushed 21 feet of storm water into Gulfport's waterfront areas and nearly destroyed the port. Katrina in August 2005 brought winds of at least 100 miles per hour and a surge of at least 19 feet, and 9,571 houses were damaged or destroyed.

Many homes you see today were rebuilt or repaired after 2005. If you own one, ask what work was permitted, who did it, and whether the paperwork is in a drawer. Buyers and their lenders will ask the same thing.

Who employs people in Gulfport, and why does it matter to a seller?

Hospitals, the military, schools and casinos carry the local job market, and steady employers keep a base of renters and buyers in town. Gulfport's 2020 annual financial report listed these as the largest employers in the city:

EmployerEmployees (2020)
Memorial Hospital4,953

Gulfport School District2,724
Harrison County School District2,086
Island View Casino1,976

The Port of Gulfport, the Gulfport Combat Readiness Training Center and Gulfport-Biloxi International Airport add to the picture.

Gulfport is served by the Gulfport School District and the Harrison County School District, and the Harrison County campus of Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College is in the city. Which district a house falls into depends on the address, so confirm it with the district before you tell a buyer.

How does the Gulf Coast climate affect a house here?

Gulfport has a humid subtropical climate that the Gulf of Mexico moderates, so summers are long and humid while extreme heat is less common than inland. NOAA normals for the Gulfport-Biloxi station show about 62.82 inches of rain a year over roughly 116 days, with July the wettest month at 7.21 inches.

The mean daily high is 90.7 degrees in August, and the all-time record of 107 degrees was set on August 26, 2023. Tropical storms are the main severe weather risk. Frequent rain and heat put steady stress on a few parts of a home:

  • Roof coverings, flashing and vents after wind events.
  • Air conditioning systems that run most of the year.
  • Wood trim, siding and crawl spaces where moisture collects.
  • Windows and doors that need to seal against driven rain.

An owner who has deferred this kind of work may find that a traditional sale stalls at inspection. That is one reason some Gulfport sellers look at an as-is cash sale instead.

What does Gulfport code enforcement do about neglected property?

The city checks properties for compliance with state law, city ordinances and zoning rules, and it says it emphasizes voluntary compliance. Complaints come in through the 311 system, by phone at (228) 868-5718, or from staff who find problems during their rounds. An officer typically visits within 24 hours to confirm whether a violation exists.

Gulfport applies the International Property Maintenance Code with a local amendment adopted as Ordinance 2812. Inspectors look at the outside of the property. They need your signed consent to enter, or a court warrant if access is denied and necessary.

The city's FAQ lays out what happens next:

  • You can ask the inspector listed on your compliance letter for more time, and extensions are routinely granted for hiring a contractor or special circumstances.
  • You can meet the inspector on site to go over a violation, and you can contest charges at a council hearing before the hearing or court date.
  • If violations are not resolved, the city can issue a citation or correct the problem itself through the City Council process, which may lead to fines or a lien on the property.

A lien from city cleanup has to be dealt with at or before closing. Read any notice you have received, and keep your response in writing.

What do Gulfport sellers owe in property taxes, and when?

Harrison County bills real property taxes on December 1, and they are due by February 1 without interest. Interest of one half percent per month starts on February 2. The county accepts payments until the Friday before its tax sale, which is held on the last Monday of August.

The Mississippi Department of Revenue explains the math as true value times assessment ratio times millage rate. A single-family, owner-occupied home is Class I at 10 percent of true value, while other real property is Class II at 15 percent. Tax Assessors must revalue real property at least once every four years.

Due without interestFebruary 1

The county's land redemption page warns that paying back taxes on a property does not make you its owner, and that a property sold at tax sale stays with the owner until the redemption period ends. If you are behind on taxes, a sale should account for the balance. Homeowners 65 or older and totally disabled owners who qualify for homestead exemption are exempt on the first $75,000 of true value, so check whether yours is on file.

What are the ways to sell a house in Gulfport?

You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer, and each route moves at a different speed. Mississippi law requires a seller of covered residential property to deliver a written property condition disclosure statement to the buyer as soon as practicable before title transfers, under Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code. Ask your agent or attorney whether your sale falls under those sections.

A deed is recorded with the Harrison County Chancery Clerk, and a title search usually happens before closing. Outstanding liens, unpaid taxes and heirs who never signed off are the most common reasons a Gulfport closing slips.

A cash sale to an investor can skip showings, listing repairs and lender appraisal delays. The tradeoff is that the offer reflects the buyer's repair costs, so compare it with what a listing would net after commissions and repairs. We do not promise a price here, and an offer is only an offer until you sign.

More questions about Gulfport, MS

Is Gulfport the county seat of Harrison County?

Yes, Gulfport is one of two county seats. Harrison County moved its seat to Gulfport in 1902, and the county's Chancery Clerk keeps land records in both Gulfport and Biloxi.

When are property taxes due in Gulfport?

Property taxes are due by February 1 each year without interest. Harrison County mails bills on December 1, and interest of 0.5 percent per month begins on February 2.

Can a house in Gulfport be sold with code violations?

Yes. Open violations or city cleanup liens usually have to be resolved, disclosed or paid from proceeds at closing, so ask the code office what is outstanding. Gulfport's inspectors will generally discuss an extension if you contact the officer on your notice.

What happens if I miss the Harrison County tax sale deadline?

The property is listed for the tax sale on the last Monday of August and offered to registered tax purchasers. You remain the legal owner during the two-year redemption period, but you must pay the taxes, interest and fees to redeem.

Does hurricane damage history affect selling in Gulfport?

It can. Katrina damaged or destroyed 9,571 houses in the city, so buyers and insurers often ask about past repairs, elevation and permits. Gather any records you have before listing or asking for a cash offer.

Where is Southaven, and why do so many sellers there think of Memphis?

Southaven is a DeSoto County city on the Mississippi side of the Tennessee line, about 14 miles south of downtown Memphis. It is a principal city of the Greater Memphis area, so many homeowners work, shop and fly out of Tennessee while paying taxes in Mississippi.

The 2020 census counted 54,648 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2024 estimate of 57,493 made Southaven the third-largest city in Mississippi and the largest Memphis suburb by population. It covers about 41.5 square miles. Interstate 55, which also carries the I-69 designation, runs through it north to south, with U.S. 51 and Mississippi Highway 302 as other main roads.

Memphis International Airport is about two miles north of the city's center point, and the city's name comes from its position south of Whitehaven, a Memphis neighborhood.

How did Southaven grow, and what does that mean for the houses?

Southaven began as a village of residential subdivisions and was incorporated in 1980. Memphis homebuilder Kemmons Wilson, who founded Holiday Inn, planned subdivisions of small starter homes just over the state line.

Growth was quick. In about 20 years Southaven doubled its land area while its population tripled. Interstate 55 through the city in the 1970s made commuting easy, and the I-69 designation was added in 2007. A large open-air shopping center, Southaven Towne Center, opened in October 2007, and Tanger Outlets Southaven opened in November 2015.

The result is a city of subdivisions from several decades. Houses built in different decades carry different repair needs, and a seller usually learns about them from the buyer's inspection report. A house that struggles through inspection is where an as-is cash sale tends to come up.

What should a Southaven seller know about weather and climate?

Southaven has a humid subtropical climate with nearly 55 inches of rain a year, spread through the year, and April is the wettest month. The average high is 49 degrees in January and 92 degrees in July.

Severe storms are part of local history. An EF-2 tornado touched down in Southaven on February 5, 2008, during the Super Tuesday outbreak and damaged numerous buildings, though no one was killed in the city. Hot summers, steady rain and storm damage together make roof condition and drainage the first things most buyers' inspectors check.

  • Roofs: look for lifted shingles and granule loss after storm seasons.
  • Drainage: standing water near the slab or crawl space often shows up in inspections.
  • HVAC: long cooling seasons put heavy wear on air conditioners.

Air traffic is another local factor. Flight paths from both north-south runways at Memphis International lead directly over the city, so buyers sometimes ask about noise.

Which schools and services serve a Southaven home?

The DeSoto County School District serves Southaven. Its schools in the city include Southaven High School, DeSoto Central High School, Southaven Middle School, DeSoto Central Middle School and Southaven Intermediate School, along with several elementary schools.

Higher education nearby includes a University of Mississippi campus in DeSoto County and Northwest Mississippi Community College. Southaven does not have a separate public transit system. It is close to the Memphis Area Transit Authority's service area, which covers Memphis and its suburbs but not Southaven, so most residents drive.

The Southaven Police Department has 139 full-time sworn officers and 31 civilian staff. The Southaven Fire Department operates four stations around the clock and provides advanced life support. Baptist Hospital-DeSoto, which opened in 1988 and added an eleven-story tower in 2006, is a major local landmark.

How are Southaven property taxes billed and paid?

DeSoto County bills the tax, and it is due by February 1 for the preceding assessment year. If the date falls on a weekend or holiday, you have until the following Monday without penalty or interest.

Mississippi assesses an owner-occupied single-family home at 10 percent of true value, and other real property such as a rental at 15 percent. The county, city and school district each set a millage rate that is applied to the assessed value. A bill that rises can come from a higher value, a higher millage or both, according to the Department of Revenue.

  • You can pay in person at the Tax Collector's offices in Hernando, Olive Branch or Horn Lake, by mail, or online.
  • The DeSoto County Tax Collector's number is 662-469-8030.
  • The county holds its tax sale on the last Monday in August, using an online bidding platform run with GovEase.

Missing the August sale has real consequences. Rankin and Lee County officials both describe a two-year window after a tax sale in which the owner can redeem the property, after which it passes to the buyer or the State, so ask the DeSoto office to confirm how redemption works before you rely on it. A tax sale on a house you are trying to sell also clouds the title and usually has to be cleared before closing.

Anyone who disagrees with an assessment can ask for a hearing with the Board of Supervisors, normally by the first Monday in August before the tax is due. Contact the Chancery Clerk for the process.

What happens to homestead exemption when a Southaven house sells?

The seller's exemption does not transfer. A new owner must apply to the county Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1, and DeSoto County notes that the exemption is not automatic.

The state requires the applicant to own and occupy the house as a primary residence on January 1, with the deed filed at the Chancery Clerk before January 7. Under that rule, a buyer closing in the spring will likely wait until the next tax year, while a buyer who closed in December can apply in time.

Exemption tiers include a credit of up to $300 for owners under 65, an exemption on the first $7,500 of assessed value for owners 65 or older or totally disabled, and full exemption for certain veterans and surviving spouses. Because a missed filing or an income tax problem can cost the exemption, a seller who also owns a second house should check that only one property carries it.

What are the rules on permits, disclosure and selling as is in Southaven?

Southaven's Building Department issues permits and examines plans, and the phone is 662-393-4639. The city's FAQ says a homeowner may submit the building permit for their own home but must hire a Mississippi state licensed contractor for trade work.

That matters for sellers who started a project and stopped. Unfinished permitted work can stall a sale, so ask the Building Department whether anything is open before you list or accept an offer.

On disclosure, Section 89-1-503 of the Mississippi Code requires the seller to deliver a written property condition disclosure statement as soon as practicable before title transfers. If it arrives after an offer is made, the buyer gets three days after hand delivery or five days after mailing to cancel the offer.

A cash purchase as is does not remove that duty. It changes who pays for the repairs. Cash Home Buyers works with Southaven sellers who would rather sell the house in its present condition than manage contractors, and we explain the terms in writing before anyone commits.

Can I sell a house in Southaven, MS without making repairs?

Yes. Mississippi does not require repairs before sale, but you must give the buyer the written property condition disclosure statement. Buyers who purchase as is account for repairs in what they pay.

When are DeSoto County property taxes due?

They are due by February 1 for the preceding assessment year, with a grace to the following Monday if that date falls on a weekend or holiday.

When does DeSoto County hold its tax sale?

The Tax Collector holds the sale on the last Monday in August each year, using an online bidding platform.

Does the buyer keep my homestead exemption?

No. A buyer must apply on their own between January 1 and April 1, and must own and occupy the home on January 1 of the tax year.

Is there public transit in Southaven?

Southaven has no separate transit system of its own. It sits near the Memphis Area Transit Authority service area, which does not include Southaven, and most residents rely on cars and I-55.

Where is Hattiesburg and how does the city sit across two counties?

Hattiesburg is the county seat of Forrest County and the anchor of the Pine Belt in south Mississippi. Most of the city is in Forrest County, and a smaller western portion, much of it commercial land gained in a 2008 annexation, is in Lamar County.

That split matters to a seller. The tax collector, the tax assessor and the chancery clerk you deal with depend on which county your parcel is in. The 2020 census counted 48,730 residents in a city that covers 54.3 square miles, and it is the principal city of a metropolitan area that includes Covington, Forrest, Lamar and Perry counties.

Hattiesburg sits at the meeting of the Leaf and Bouie rivers, about 90 miles southeast of Jackson and 74 miles north of Biloxi. Interstate 59, U.S. 49, U.S. 98 and U.S. 11 all serve the city, and the city runs its own bus system, Hub City Transit, from an intermodal depot downtown that also handles Amtrak's Crescent.

How did Hattiesburg grow, and what does that mean for older houses?

Hattiesburg was founded in 1882 by civil engineer William H. Hardy, who named it for his wife Hattie, and it was incorporated in 1884. Railroads made it a trading center, which is where the nickname "The Hub City" comes from. The Gulf and Ship Island Railroad, finished through the city, set off a lumber boom in 1897.

The city has a historic core and a long list of older streets, and it also has land added by annexation on the west side. The city has a Historic Conservation Commission and a design guidelines manual for historic districts, so a house in one of those districts may need a Certificate of Appropriateness before exterior work. Ask the city's planning office at 601-545-4599 whether a particular address is covered.

Older homes bring familiar repair items: original wiring, galvanized or cast iron plumbing, and foundations that have settled. A buyer's lender may balk at these. An investor buying for cash usually does not.

What drives Hattiesburg's economy and housing demand?

Universities, health care, manufacturing and the military training base at Camp Shelby give Hattiesburg more than one source of demand. The University of Southern Mississippi and William Carey University both have their main campuses here, and Camp Shelby, south of the city, is the largest National Guard training base east of the Mississippi River and hosts up to 100,000 Guardsmen and Reservists a year.

What is the severe weather risk for a Hattiesburg house?

Tornadoes are the standout hazard. Hattiesburg has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and short, mild winters, and spring thunderstorms can bring lightning, heavy rain, large hail and tornadoes.

Two recent events are on the record. An EF4 tornado on February 10, 2013 formed in Lamar County and moved east into Hattiesburg, causing EF1 to EF3 damage on the south side of the University of Southern Mississippi campus and in neighborhoods just north of downtown. On January 21, 2017, an EF3 tornado struck early in the morning, killing four and injuring 20, and about 10,000 people lost power.

  • Insurance claim files, contractor invoices and permits should stay with the house paperwork.

The Urban Development Department handles planning, zoning, permits, building inspections and code enforcement from City Hall at 200 Forrest Street. The building division number is 601-554-1003 and code enforcement is 601-554-1027.

Zoning follows the city's Land Development Code, and the building code is the 2018 International Residential Code. Permitted work must be inspected before it is covered, and the city asks for at least 24 hours of notice for an inspection.

The city's residential page notes that an owner who acts as his or her own contractor on a single-family home may be subject to the Mississippi Home Warranty Act and, if the home is later sold, may be required to warrant it for up to seven years from the sale date. If you built or added to your home yourself, talk with an attorney before you sell.

The city also publishes information on floodplain management. If your property is near the Leaf or Bouie rivers, ask about its flood designation.

Both counties collect property taxes by February 1 each year. The Forrest County Tax Collector at 601 N. Main Street in downtown Hattiesburg describes taxes as due by February 1, and Lamar County gives February 1 as the last day to pay without interest.

Forrest County explains that the tax assessor appraises property, the board of supervisors reviews the rolls after a protest period, and then the collector applies the assessment ratios and the levy set by the board and the City of Hattiesburg. The county also notes that after you buy a property it can take up to a year for the new deed to be reflected on the tax map, because the mapper works the previous year's recorded deeds.

Most of Hattiesburg is in Forrest County, which is the county seat. A western portion of the city is in Lamar County, so confirm the county for your parcel.

Forrest County property taxes are due by February 1 of each year. The Tax Collector's office is at 601 N. Main Street in Hattiesburg and takes payments online as well.

Generally a permit is required to repair or alter an existing residence, but certain routine repairs may not need one. Call the building division at 601-554-1003 before starting work.

Yes. You can sell it as is, but you should disclose known damage and keep insurance and repair records. Cash buyers often take storm-damaged houses that lenders will not finance.

Biloxi is a Gulf Coast city in Harrison County, Mississippi, with the Mississippi Sound along its southern edge and Biloxi Bay on the northeast side. Gulfport borders it on the west, D'Iberville on the north and east, and Ocean Springs sits across the bay in Jackson County.

Water runs through the middle of the city too. The Back Bay of Biloxi crosses it from the Jackson County line toward Big Lake, and the Tchoutacabouffa River forms part of the eastern boundary. Wikipedia's city profile lists the elevation at 20 feet, which explains why flood zones come up early in almost every Biloxi sale.

What in Biloxi's history shapes the housing stock?

Biloxi's housing carries layers of coastal history. The Biloxi Lighthouse was finished on site in May 1848, and by the late 1800s the city was both a summer resort and a seafood town, with the first cannery opening in 1881.

Keesler Field was built during World War II and is now Keesler Air Force Base, home to the 81st Training Wing and the 403rd Wing of the Air Force Reserve. Legal gambling in the 1990s brought the resort casinos.

Storms are the other thread. By the measure of storm surge at the Biloxi Lighthouse, the most destructive hurricanes struck in 1855, 1906, 1909, 1947, 1969 (Camille) and 2005. Katrina came ashore on August 29, 2005 with a storm surge of about 30 feet. Houses here are therefore a mix of pre-1969 survivors, post-Katrina rebuilds and newer elevated construction, and a buyer or inspector will ask which one yours is.

Biloxi has a humid subtropical climate, and the numbers show why roofs, air conditioning and moisture control dominate repair lists. NOAA normals reproduced by Wikipedia put average annual rainfall at 66.80 inches, spread over about 111 days with measurable precipitation.

The more important rule for sellers is the 50 percent test. A storm-damaged house in a mapped flood zone can therefore cost far more to repair for resale than the visible damage suggests.

  • Ask whether the work would count toward the 50 percent threshold.
  • Confirm any contractor holds a City of Biloxi license, which the city specifically recommends after storms.

The city flood bulletin is an older document, and FEMA's updated flood elevation maps took effect in May 2009, so confirm current requirements with the city. You can read the city's flood map page for background. Biloxi also operates an environmental court, according to the City of Clinton's community development page, which handles property maintenance and code cases.

Keesler Air Force Base sits inside the city limits, and eight casinos operate in Biloxi, including Beau Rivage, Golden Nugget Biloxi, Hard Rock Hotel and Casino and Harrah's Gulf Coast. A job change or new orders can set a firm moving date, and sellers in that spot often weigh a direct cash sale against a listing on timing alone.

A Mississippi seller of most residential property must hand the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement as soon as practicable before title transfers. Recording comes next. The Harrison County Chancery Clerk records deeds, deeds of trust, releases and liens. When does a cash offer make sense for a Biloxi house?

A cash offer tends to fit when the house needs more work than a lender or retail buyer will accept, or when time matters more than squeezing out the last dollar.   • An inherited home where the heirs live elsewhere and want to settle the estate.
  • A rental with a tenant or a vacancy that has become a monthly drain.
  • A move on a deadline, such as a job change or new orders.

A cash sale still involves a purchase contract, a title search and a deed recorded with the Chancery Clerk. Compare any figure against what a repaired, listed sale would net after repairs, commissions and carrying costs.

Taxes are due by February 1 each year without interest. The county tax collector says bills are mailed December 1 and interest of 0.5 percent per month begins February 2. Unpaid real property goes to the tax sale on the last Monday of August.

Do I need to give a buyer a disclosure statement in Mississippi?

Yes, for property covered by Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code. The statement is due as soon as practicable before title transfers, and a buyer who receives it after making an offer has three days after hand delivery, or five after mailing, to withdraw.

Where are deeds recorded for a Biloxi property?

They are recorded with the Harrison County Chancery Clerk. The Judicial District 2 recording office is at 730 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Biloxi, and a deed costs $26.00 for the first five pages in Harrison County under the clerk's published fee schedule.

Does homeowner's insurance cover flooding in Biloxi?

No. The city's flood bulletin states that standard homeowner's policies exclude flood damage. A separate National Flood Insurance Program policy is available, and Biloxi's participation in the Community Rating System gives policyholders a premium discount.

Can I sell a house in Biloxi that is behind on taxes?

Yes, as long as the sale closes before the tax sale. Harrison County will not accept real property payments once the sale begins, and the Friday before the sale at 5:00 p.m. is the cutoff.

How did Olive Branch grow so quickly?

Those are countywide figures, and the list includes sites outside Olive Branch itself.

The city's own mayor leans on the industrial base. Mayor Ken Adams started the Olive Branch Mayor's Industrial Council in late 2025, which brings together about 40 of the city's largest employers once a quarter. Those taxes help fund schools, the library and infrastructure. For a home seller, the useful point is that nearby land can change use as industrial projects move forward, so check what is planned near your address.

Mississippi's homestead exemption has three tiers. The regular tier gives qualified owners under 65 a tax credit of up to $300. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, are exempt from tax on the first $7,500 of assessed value. Certain disabled veterans and surviving spouses are exempt from all property tax on their homestead. DeSoto County lists a 2027 filing window from January 4 to April 1 at the Tax Assessor's office in Hernando. A buyer's circumstances can change the exemption, so a new owner may need to reapply.

Recording fees at the chancery clerk are set by statute, and DeSoto County provides a fee calculator on its land records page.

Olive Branch sellers can list through an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer. A well-kept house can do well on the open market. A cash sale is more useful when the house needs work, when you have a tenant, or when you must move soon.

If a bill goes unpaid, penalties and interest accrue. Pearl was incorporated late. Residents voted on incorporation in 1968, the name was picked in January 1969, and the Mississippi Supreme Court ordered the city's incorporation on June 5, 1973, with the charter presented on June 29, 1973.

Before that the area was a railroad and school community called Pearson, then Pearl, with a one-room school petitioned for in 1911. Suburban growth out of Jackson in the 1960s drove most of the housing stock. The Pearl Municipal Separate School District was created by city ordinance in 1976.

The Mississippi disclosure statement covers the condition of the property, and a seller who delivers it late gives the buyer a right to cancel. Keep records of repairs and insurance claims, and ask a Mississippi real estate attorney how to answer specific questions.

That ratio gap is a practical concern for landlords here. A rental house is taxed on a larger share of its value than a house its owner lives in, and a house that stops being owner-occupied can lose its homestead credit. Assessors must revalue real property at least every four years, and a value dispute goes to the county Board of Supervisors, normally by the first Monday in August before the tax is due.

What should a seller know about homestead exemption and taxes at closing?

Homestead exemption is tied to the owner who lives in the house on January 1, so it does not pass to the next owner. Each new owner has to apply at the Tax Assessor's office between January 1 and April 1.

The state's eligibility rules include owning and occupying the house as a primary residence on January 1, with the deed filed with the Chancery Clerk before January 7. The regular tier gives a credit of up to $300 for owners under 65. Owners 65 or older or totally disabled are exempt on the first $7,500 of assessed value, and some veterans and surviving spouses receive a full exemption.

For an investor buying a Starkville rental, none of this applies, because the house will not be a primary residence. For a family buying their first home, a closing in the first months of the year can mean waiting until the next year for the credit.

Unpaid taxes can lead to a tax sale. State rules allow sales on the first Monday in April and the last Monday in August, and the county Tax Collector handles the details.

What does Mississippi require a Starkville seller to disclose, and what are the sale options?

Under Section 89-1-503 of the Mississippi Code, the seller gives the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement as soon as practicable before title transfers. If the buyer receives it after making an offer, the buyer has three days after hand delivery, or five days after mailing, to withdraw the offer in writing.

A Starkville owner generally has three paths. The first is a retail listing, which can work well near campus when the house is in good order and the calendar is right. The second is selling to another investor, which suits a rental with tenants. The third is a direct as-is sale to a cash buyer, which skips repairs, showings and lender conditions.

Starkville's history is also tied to the university. The area was chosen for the agricultural college because of its farming, timber, cattle and dairy output, and the city later became a college town. If a house has been in a family for years, old deeds, unrecorded transfers and shared heirs are worth checking during the title search.

Whatever you choose, order a title search. An attorney or title company can find unpaid taxes, mortgages and liens, and prepare the deed. The Chancery Clerk records the deed, and it needs a notarized seller signature and a legal description.

Can I sell a Starkville rental house with tenants in it?

Yes. The buyer takes the house subject to the existing lease, so you need to hand over the lease, deposit information and rent records. Some buyers prefer a vacant house, so talk through timing before you commit.

When are Oktibbeha County property taxes due?

They are due on or before February 1 for property assessed in the preceding year. If February 1 falls on a weekend or holiday, payment the next Monday carries no penalty.

Is a Starkville rental taxed differently from a home I live in?

Yes. Under the Mississippi Constitution an owner-occupied single-family home is assessed at 10 percent of true value, while other real property is assessed at 15 percent.

Which school district covers Starkville?

The Starkville Oktibbeha Consolidated School District, formed in 2015 by merging the former Starkville and Oktibbeha County districts.

Do I have to disclose problems when I sell in Mississippi?

Most sellers must deliver a written property condition disclosure statement before title transfers. A buyer who gets it late can cancel the offer within three days of hand delivery or five days of mailing.
